docs.title: 🧪 3. Test a Node
docs.text: In a run started with mujou.run, dt follows the real time that passes, and the order in which the nodes update differs every time, so the results differ slightly from run to run. This page tests the node of 2. Write a Node with mujou.testing, which runs nodes with the same result every time.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Import it with import mujou.testing; import mujou alone does not.

Name Role mujou.testing.run(root, ...) Runs the tree with the timer, inputs and state of mujou.run (no workers) and returns a ManualRun. No node updates until step updates it. It runs on a new mujou.time.VirtualTimer by default ManualRun.step(dt, *nodes) Moves the timer dt seconds forward, then updates the given nodes once each, in the given order ManualRun.timer The run's VirtualTimer

ManualRun is a Run, so write, read, state_dict and the rest work as with mujou.run.

docs.title: A test
docs.text:
class TestLeaky:
    def test_follows_the_exact_solution(self) -> None:
        tau, h, steps = 0.1, 0.001, 100
        node = Leaky(tau)
        one = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float64)
        expected = 0.0
        with mujou.testing.run(node, inputs={node.prev: one}) as run:
            for _ in range(steps):
                run.step(h)  # 1 ms later, then every node once (period is ignored)
                expected += (1 - math.exp(-h / tau)) * (1.0 - expected)
            y, t = run.read_with_time(node.next)
        assert t is not None and t.ns == steps * 1_000_000  # sent at the last step
        torch.testing.assert_close(y, torch.tensor(expected, dtype=torch.float64))

uv run pytest examples/test_leaky.py
  1. mujou.testing.run(node, inputs=...) runs the node on a new VirtualTimer at time 0. inputs are the values of the input ports from the start
  2. Each run.step(h) moves the time h seconds forward and updates every node once, so the dt of the node is exactly h
  3. The reference is the exact solution, computed with the same coefficient. Compare it with torch.testing.assert_close, or with torch.equal when the reference does the same operations in the same order (below)
  4. The time the node sent the output is steps milliseconds: no real time enters a manual run

docs.title: The order of the updates
docs.text:
class TestLeakyChain:
    def test_follows_the_discrete_algorithm(self) -> None:
        tau, h, steps = 0.01, 0.001, 50
        u = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float64)
        # The reference: the discrete algorithm, a then b at every step.
        a, b = SCALAR.zeros(), SCALAR.zeros()
        for _ in range(steps):
            a += (1 - math.exp(-h / tau)) * (u - a)
            b += (1 - math.exp(-h / tau)) * (a - b)  # b reads the new a

        net = LeakyChain(tau)
        with mujou.testing.run(net, inputs={net.prev: u}) as run:
            for _ in range(steps):
                run.step(h, net.a, net.b)  # a, then b, which reads a's new value
            y = run.read(net.next)
        assert torch.equal(y, b)  # the same operations: equal to the last bit
  • step(dt) without nodes updates every node once, in the order of the tree (the order the attributes were assigned)
  • The order changes the result. With step(h, net.a, net.b), b reads the value a sent in this step; with step(h, net.b, net.a), the one from the step before
  • A node's dt is the time since its last update, the first from the start of the run. A node passed twice in one step updates once: the second time is skipped, since its time has not moved
  • The period of a node is not used in a manual run
  • A node that raises makes step raise NetworkError at once

docs.title: Save and restore
docs.text:
A run that takes the state midway and goes on in a new instance matches a run that went on without stopping, to the last bit:

def run_steps(n: int, state: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a new ``LeakyChain`` for ``n`` steps of 1 ms and return its state."""
    net = LeakyChain(0.01)
    u = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float64)
    with mujou.testing.run(net, inputs={net.prev: u}, state=state) as run:
        for _ in range(n):
            run.step(0.001)
    return run.state_dict()


class TestRestore:
    def test_a_restored_run_goes_on_as_one_that_did_not_stop(self) -> None:
        straight = run_steps(20)
        # Ten steps, then ten more in a new instance restored from the first half,
        # on a VirtualTimer of its own that starts at the time of the state.
        resumed = run_steps(10, state=run_steps(10))
        x = resumed["nodes"]["b"]["state"]["x"]
        assert torch.equal(x, straight["nodes"]["b"]["state"]["x"])

A run restored from a state runs on a VirtualTimer of its own, which starts at the time of the state.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
When a node raises, step raises NetworkError, whose __cause__ is the node's exception. Every later call of the run raises it again, including the shutdown at the end of the with block, so put pytest.raises around the whole block, in the same with statement:

with pytest.raises(NetworkError) as info, mujou.testing.run(net) as run:
    run.step(0.001)  # a node raises ValueError here
assert isinstance(info.value.__cause__, ValueError)

docs.title: Other conditions for determinism
docs.text:
• Give a seed to the nodes that draw random numbers, and draw them from self.generator (see Threads and Devices)
  • Move the time only with step. Nothing is sent unless step is called, so wait_for and subscribe without a timeout wait forever on the thread that steps
  • To put several runs on one time axis, pass the same mujou.time.VirtualTimer() to each: a step of one moves the others too

docs.title: 🔥 4. Learn in a Node
docs.text: This page writes a node that learns with backpropagation (BP) inside itself, from a stream whose target changes while it runs. There is no training phase and no inference phase: the node predicts and learns from each new batch as it comes.

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
A teacher node sends a batch from \(y = a x + b\) every 10 ms, with the a the host writes; the host changes a while the network runs. The learner follows its loss: it falls, jumps when the target changes, and falls again.

uv run python examples/online_learning.py

t = 0.48 s: loss = 0.000090  (learned a = 2.0)
t = 0.49 s: loss = 3.405589  (a changed at 0.48 s)
t = 0.97 s: loss = 0.000095  (learned a = -1.0)
the learner's weight = -0.988, bias = 0.498

docs.title: The learner
docs.text:
class Learner(Node):
    """Follows the gradient flow dW/dt = -rate * dL/dW, learning once from each
    new batch for the time since the last one, and sends its loss on each batch
    before learning from it."""

    MAX_STEP = 0.01  # seconds: a longer explicit Euler step could diverge

    def __init__(self, rate: float) -> None:
        # Updating more often than the teacher sends would only re-read its batch.
        super().__init__(period=0.005, seed=0)
        self.rate = rate  # a setting, not state
        self.model = nn.Linear(1, 1)  # has state_dict: in the state by itself
        # seed reproduces only self.generator: initialize the module from it.
        nn.init.normal_(self.model.weight, std=0.1, generator=self.generator)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.model.bias)
        self.last = -1  # the time (ns) of the batch learned from last
        self.elapsed = 0.0  # seconds since then
        self.register_state("last")  # plain values that change: register them
        self.register_state("elapsed")
        self.prev = Port(recv=BATCH_SPEC)
        self.loss = Port(send=SCALAR, initial=torch.tensor(math.inf))  # no batch yet

    @override
    def on_update(self, dt: float) -> None:
        super().on_update(dt)
        self.elapsed += dt
        batch, t = self.prev.recv_with_time()
        if t is None or t.ns == self.last:  # nothing sent yet, or nothing new
            return
        self.last = t.ns
        x, y = batch["x"], batch["y"]
        with torch.no_grad():  # the loss on an unseen batch needs no graph
            self.loss.send(nn.functional.mse_loss(self.model(x), y))
        # How far to learn is set by the time, not by the number of batches: move
        # by the elapsed time, in n equal steps no longer than MAX_STEP.
        n = max(1, math.ceil(self.elapsed / self.MAX_STEP))
        for _ in range(n):
            loss = nn.functional.mse_loss(self.model(x), y)  # records the graph
            loss.backward()
            with torch.no_grad():  # the step itself is not part of any graph
                for p in self.model.parameters():
                    assert p.grad is not None
                    p -= self.elapsed / n * self.rate * p.grad
                    p.grad = None
        self.elapsed = 0.0
  • The module is state. self.model has state_dict and load_state_dict, so it is in the node's state by itself, as a tensor attribute is
  • The seed. seed=0 seeds self.generator, the node's own random generator. The default initialization of nn.Linear draws from the global generator that every node shares, so initialize the weights again from self.generator
  • Plain values join the state with register_state. last and elapsed change while the node runs, but they are neither tensors nor modules: registered, they are saved and restored with the rest
  • New or not. recv_with_time() returns the batch with the time it was sent. Its time is None until the teacher first sends, and it stays the same until the teacher sends again, so the learner learns once from each batch
  • Gradients as in plain PyTorch. The hooks record gradients as plain PyTorch does: loss.backward() fills p.grad, and the parameters are updated in place inside torch.no_grad(). Values computed only to send (the loss before learning) need no graph either
  • By the time, not by the batch. The learner follows the gradient flow \(\frac{dW}{dt} = -\text{rate}\,\frac{\partial L}{\partial W}\) over the time since it last learned (elapsed), not a fixed step per batch: how far it learns depends on time, not on how often it runs. A long elapsed is split into steps no longer than MAX_STEP, so that explicit Euler does not diverge

BP stays inside the node. A port sends a copy, detached from the graph, so no gradient crosses nodes.

docs.title: Settings of torch
docs.text:
# The nodes compute on the run's worker threads, and torch adds threads of its
# own for each: keep those few (a setting of the whole process, made by the host).
torch.set_num_threads(1)

The host sets the settings of the whole process, such as the number of torch's threads, before the run. A node changes only settings of its own thread, and sets them back before its hook returns (see Threads and Devices).

docs.title: The run
docs.text:
teacher, learner = Teacher(), Learner(rate=5.0)
teacher.next.connect(learner.prev)
net = mujou.Group(teacher=teacher, learner=learner)
with mujou.run(net, inputs={teacher.a: torch.tensor(A_BEFORE)}) as run:
    # How fast the learner learns depends on time, not on how often it runs:
    # follow its loss, giving each phase up to 5 s of real time.
    loss, t = run.wait_for(learner.loss, learned, timeout=5.0)
    assert t is not None  # the loss on a batch, not the initial inf
    print(f"t = {float(t):.2f} s: loss = {loss.item():.6f}  (learned a = {A_BEFORE})")
    # The world changes: the same learner keeps learning, with no new phase.
    changed_at = run.write({teacher.a: torch.tensor(A_AFTER)})
    loss, t = run.wait_for(learner.loss, lambda loss: loss.item() > 1e-2, timeout=5.0)
    assert t is not None
    print(
        f"t = {float(t):.2f} s: loss = {loss.item():.6f}  (a changed at {float(changed_at):.2f} s)"
    )
    loss, t = run.wait_for(learner.loss, learned, timeout=5.0)
    assert t is not None
    print(f"t = {float(t):.2f} s: loss = {loss.item():.6f}  (learned a = {A_AFTER})")

# After the run, the nodes' attributes are the host's to read.
weight, bias = learner.model.weight.item(), learner.model.bias.item()
print(f"the learner's weight = {weight:.3f}, bias = {bias:.3f}")

run.wait_for follows the loss port until the condition holds. After the run, the nodes' attributes are the host's to read: learner.model is the module the learner learned.

docs.title: 🧠 5. Learn with PC-ALM
docs.text: The module mujou.pc learns a PyTorch model split into nodes with PC-ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Predictive Coding, https://pub.sakana.ai/pc-alm/). Each node holds a part of the model and learns from its neighbors' messages only; at equilibrium, its gradients are those of backpropagation. This page learns a regression with it. What you choose are the time constants and how long each batch is shown.

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
uv run python examples/pc_regression.py

batch   1: loss 0.4157 (the mean of the last 1)
batch  50: loss 0.0458 (the mean of the last 50)
...
batch 300: loss 0.0060 (the mean of the last 50)

docs.title: The chain
docs.text:
SHOWN = 0.032  # seconds of the run's timer each batch is shown
# tau.h sets how fast the activities relax (and the period of the nodes, h / 4),
# and the weights learn once per batch, by SGD at the rate SHOWN / theta = 0.3.
tau = pc.TimeConstants(h=4e-3, lam=8e-3, theta=SHOWN / 0.3)
torch.manual_seed(0)  # the initial weights, before the run
net = pc.Chain(
    nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 64), nn.Tanh()),
    nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 64), nn.Tanh()),
    nn.Linear(64, 1),
    x=TensorSpec((B, 2)),
    y=TensorSpec((B, 1)),
    batch=B,
    loss=pc.MSELoss(B),  # the loss of each sample, (B,)
    tau=tau,
    learn_interval=0.75 * SHOWN,  # learn once, 3/4 of the way through each batch
)

pc.Chain makes one node for each module and connects them in order, as nn.Sequential computes them: a pc.Input that takes the samples, a pc.Layer for each module but the last (layer0, layer1), and a pc.Output for the last, with the loss. The children of the chain are input, layer0, layer1 and output, which are also their paths in the state; net.layers gives the layers in order, net.layers[0] being layer0.

  • x and y are the specs of the inputs and targets, and batch is the shape they start with: B samples here. Without batch, the chain takes one sample at a time, and x and y would be TensorSpec((2,)) and TensorSpec((1,))
  • loss returns the loss of each sample, of the shape of the batch: pc.MSELoss(B) (the mean squared error of each sample, averaged over its dimensions as nn.MSELoss does) or pc.CrossEntropyLoss(B), or a function of your own that returns that shape. Give the loss the same batch as the chain (the batch)
  • tau holds the time constants, in seconds of the run's timer: h for the activities (every node of the chain updates once every tau.period, which is tau.h / 4), lam for the duals and theta for the weights
  • learn_interval is when the nodes learn, counted from each write: here once per batch, three quarters of the way through it. A learning step weighs the time since the node last learned, so with one step per batch, the learning rate per batch is the showing time divided by tau.theta. It has no default: None learns in every update, for a stream whose input changes at every frame, and good values for that mode have not been measured yet

Inside a node, the module is differentiated by autograd, as in BP. Initialize the weights when you make the modules (here from torch.manual_seed in the host, before the run); the nodes do not.

docs.title: Show and learn
docs.text:
torch.set_num_threads(1)
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)
every = torch.ones(B, dtype=torch.bool)  # every sample has a target
losses: list[float] = []
with mujou.run(net) as run:
    for i in range(300):
        x = 2 * torch.rand(B, 2, generator=g) - 1
        y = torch.sin(2 * x[:, :1]) * torch.cos(x[:, 1:])
        p = pc.show(run, net, pc.Sample(x=x, y=y, mask=every), seconds=SHOWN)
        losses.append(nn.functional.mse_loss(p["y_hat"], y).item())  # before learning
        if i == 0 or (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
            recent = losses[-50:]
            mean = sum(recent) / len(recent)
            print(
                f"batch {i + 1:3d}: loss {mean:.4f} (the mean of the last {len(recent)})"
            )
    # The state of a node, by its path: input, layer0, layer1, output.
    lam = run.state_dict()["nodes"]["layer0"]["state"]["lam"]
print(f"the mean |lam| of layer0 (its credit) at the end: {lam.abs().mean():.2e}")

pc.show(run, net, sample, seconds=SHOWN) writes the batch, waits for the first prediction the chain makes for it, and returns that prediction once the batch has been shown for SHOWN seconds of the run's timer. Meanwhile the nodes relax towards the target and learn from it. The prediction comes before any node has learned from the batch, so its loss measures how well the model predicts data it has not seen yet (the prequential loss).

  • mask says which samples have a target. A sample whose mask is False adds nothing to the loss: with every mask False, no weight moves (the activities still do), which is how to evaluate the same running chain. There is no inference mode to switch to
  • A pc.Prediction holds y_hat with the y, mask and time of the sample it was made from, so a prediction always pairs with its own target
  • run.state_dict()["nodes"]["layer0"]["state"] is the state of the first layer: its activity h, its dual lam (the credit of backpropagation at equilibrium), its module and its clock, and what it keeps to move h when its prediction jumps (mu, jump, jumped, jumps and seen_jumps, explained in PC-ALM)

docs.title: 💾 6. Save and Resume
docs.text: This page takes the state of a run, saves it, and resumes from it in a new run. What the state holds is in How Mujou Works.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
"""Save the state of a run, and restore it in a new run that goes on from there.

A node collects its state by itself: every attribute that holds a
``torch.Tensor`` or an ``nn.Module``, and the state of its generator.
``Run.state_dict`` gathers the states of all nodes, the latest messages and the
time into one tree, a plain ``dict`` of CPU tensors. Save it with ``torch.save``
(or pickle), and read it back with ``torch.load``.
"""

import io
from typing import override

import torch
from torch import nn

import mujou
import mujou.time
from mujou import Node, Port, TensorSpec

VECTOR1 = TensorSpec((1,))


class Integrator(Node):
    """Integrates its input over time (dx/dt = u) and sends ``readout(x)``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.x = VECTOR1.zeros()  # a tensor: part of the state
        self.readout = nn.Linear(1, 1)  # a module: part of the state
        self.prev = Port(recv=VECTOR1)
        self.next = Port(send=VECTOR1)

    @override
    def on_update(self, dt: float) -> None:
        super().on_update(dt)
        self.x += dt * self.prev.recv()  # in place: other references to x stay valid
        with torch.no_grad():  # computed only to send: no graph
            self.next.send(self.readout(self.x))


class Model(mujou.Network):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.integrator = Integrator()
        self.prev = self.integrator.prev
        self.next = self.integrator.next


one = torch.ones(1)

# Run for a while, then stop and take the state at the end.
net = Model()
with mujou.run(net, inputs={net.prev: one}) as run:
    run.timer.sleep(0.2)
tree = run.state_dict()  # after a normal end: the state at the stop
saved = tree["nodes"]["integrator"]["state"]  # this node's state_dict()
print("state of the node:", {k: type(v).__name__ for k, v in saved.items()})
file = io.BytesIO()  # or a path, such as "state.pt"
# Every tensor of the tree is on the CPU, so torch.load needs no GPU (a CUDA node's
# generator state still restores only into a CUDA node).
torch.save(tree, file)

# A new instance of the same network goes on from the saved state and time. A
# network runs once: run the one the tree came from again, and mujou.run raises.
restored = Model()
file.seek(0)
loaded = torch.load(file)  # the default weights_only=True reads the plain dict
with mujou.run(restored, inputs={restored.prev: one}, state=loaded) as run:
    # On a timer of its own that starts at the time of the tree: the global timer
    # and the other runs do not go back.
    assert run.timer is not mujou.time.global_timer
    print(f"restored at t = {float(run.timer.now()):.3f} s of its own timer")
    run.timer.sleep(0.1)
after = run.state_dict()["nodes"]["integrator"]["state"]

x0, x1 = saved["x"].item(), after["x"].item()
print(f"x = {x0:.3f} at the save, {x1:.3f} after 0.1 s more")
# The integral went on from the saved value: from 0, it would be about 0.1. (How
# far it gets in 0.2 s and 0.1 s depends on when the last update falls.)
assert x1 > x0 > 0
# The module was restored too: the new instance had other random weights.
assert torch.equal(after["readout"]["weight"], saved["readout"]["weight"])
  1. The node keeps its state in attributes: self.x (a tensor) and self.readout (a module) are collected by themselves, with the state of the node's random generator
  2. It creates them in __init__ and updates them in place in on_update, so that other references to them (from an optimizer, say) keep pointing at the state (see 2. Write a Node)
  3. The host takes the tree with run.state_dict(), while the run runs or after it ended normally (here, after the with block)
  4. It saves the tree with torch.save
  5. To resume, it builds a new instance of the same network, not the one the tree came from, since a network runs once (rules a node keeps), and passes the tree as mujou.run(net, state=tree)

docs.title: The tree
docs.text:
The tree is a plain dict of copies on the CPU, keyed by the paths of the nodes: the state of each node, the latest message on each channel with its time, the time of each node's last update, and the time of the timer. Its exact shape is in the API reference of Run.state_dict.

Taking it pauses the run: each node stops between two updates, never in the middle of one, so every value in the tree is of the same time. The paused time does not enter any dt afterwards. Each node's on_pause and on_resume run around this pause, to hold its I/O meanwhile; a pause of the timer (run.timer.pause()) calls neither.

When you take it What you get While the network runs The state at that time After a normal end The values as the nodes left them after on_stop, at the time shutdown asked the run to stop After an exception Nothing: state_dict raises NetworkError. Take the state you want to keep while the network runs, regularly during a long run

docs.title: When you resume
docs.text:
• The resumed run has a timer of its own. It runs on a new Timer (run.timer) that starts at the time and the time scale of the tree, so mujou.time.global_timer and the other runs do not go back. Passing timer= with state= raises ValueError, and global_timer.pause() does not pause a resumed run: pause its run.timer
  • Build the same network. The resumed network must have the node paths, ports and connections of the one the tree came from; otherwise mujou.run raises ValueError, listing what is missing and what is in excess. Renaming an attribute changes a path, so a tree saved before the rename no longer resumes. In both cases nothing has started, and the same instances run once the tree is fixed
  • Keep the state of each node. A node state with other keys or shapes makes the default load_state_dict raise ValueError while the node starts, so mujou.run raises NetworkError (its __cause__ is the ValueError), and those instances do not run again: build new ones
  • Inputs. With both state= and inputs=, the values of inputs replace those of the tree

docs.title: Values of your own in the state
docs.text:
Tensors, objects with state_dict and load_state_dict, and the state of self.generator are collected; numbers, strings, and lists or dicts of tensors are not. For a plain value that changes while the node runs, assign the attribute in __init__ and register it:

self.elapsed = 0.0
self.register_state("elapsed")

The value goes into the state as it is, whatever you assign to the attribute later. Register only an attribute that exists (otherwise AttributeError). Keep it to types that torch.load reads with its default (int, float, bool, str, None, and lists, tuples and dicts of them, or tensors).

For the rest, such as a deque, override both state_dict and load_state_dict: extend what super().state_dict() returns, and pass super().load_state_dict the state without the keys you added.

from collections import deque
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any, override

import torch

from mujou import Node


class Recent(Node):
    """Keeps the last 8 inputs in a deque."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.recent: deque[torch.Tensor] = deque(maxlen=8)

    @override
    def state_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {**super().state_dict(), "recent": list(self.recent)}

    @override
    def load_state_dict(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.recent = deque((x.clone() for x in state["recent"]), maxlen=8)  # a copy of the tree's
        super().load_state_dict({k: v for k, v in state.items() if k != "recent"})

state_dict is called while the node is paused, and its ports refuse to receive and send there, so that taking the state is not seen by the other nodes. Mujou copies what it returns. load_state_dict is called once, after on_start and before the first on_update.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• torch.save and torch.load with its default weights_only=True read a tree made of tensors, numbers, strings, dicts, lists and tuples: what Mujou puts in it. A tree that holds objects of your own classes (from register_state or an override) does not load that way
  • pickle.load and torch.load(..., weights_only=False) can run code from the file. Do not read files you do not trust with them
  • The default load_state_dict copies each tensor to the node's device, so a machine without a GPU can read a tree saved from nodes on CUDA. The state of a random generator differs between the CPU and CUDA, though: a tree restores only into nodes on the same kind of device as the ones that saved it

docs.title: Several runs at one time
docs.text: run.state_dict() takes the state of one run at one time. To take the states of several runs on one timer at one time, pause the timer first; see Time.

docs.title: Mujou
docs.text:
連続的継続学習のための非同期分散型深層学習フレームワーク

画像は、落合陽一の作品「リキッドユニバース」をもとに新たに制作したもの

mujou は推論と学習を同時に行い続ける深層学習フレームワークである。ノードをつなぎ、ネットワークを構築する。

開発の初期段階

mujou はまだ開発の初期段階にある。API は予告なく変わることがある。

docs.location: ja/#-学び続けるネットワーク
docs.title: 🌱 学び続けるネットワーク
docs.text:
従来の機械学習は学習を終えたら重みを固定し推論する。mujou のネットワークは、実行中常に入力を受け取って出力を出し、同時に学び続ける。

学習と推論を切り替えるモードも、エポックも無い。

名前は「諸行無常」の「無常」（常が無いこと）から取った。ストリームから学び続け、常に変わり続ける機械を作るためのフレームワーク。リアルタイム処理やロボティクスのように、動きながら学ぶ用途を狙う。

次のプログラムがそのネットワーク。PC-ALM のノードの鎖が、流れてくるバッチから回帰を学ぶ（学ぶノードは 3 つ）。ノードは動き続けたまま、各バッチから学ぶ前にそのバッチを予測する。

SHOWN = 0.032  # seconds of the run's timer each batch is shown
# tau.h sets how fast the activities relax (and the period of the nodes, h / 4),
# and the weights learn once per batch, by SGD at the rate SHOWN / theta = 0.3.
tau = pc.TimeConstants(h=4e-3, lam=8e-3, theta=SHOWN / 0.3)
torch.manual_seed(0)  # the initial weights, before the run
net = pc.Chain(
    nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 64), nn.Tanh()),
    nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 64), nn.Tanh()),
    nn.Linear(64, 1),
    x=TensorSpec((B, 2)),
    y=TensorSpec((B, 1)),
    batch=B,
    loss=pc.MSELoss(B),  # the loss of each sample, (B,)
    tau=tau,
    learn_interval=0.75 * SHOWN,  # learn once, 3/4 of the way through each batch
)

torch.set_num_threads(1)
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(1)
every = torch.ones(B, dtype=torch.bool)  # every sample has a target
losses: list[float] = []
with mujou.run(net) as run:
    for i in range(300):
        x = 2 * torch.rand(B, 2, generator=g) - 1
        y = torch.sin(2 * x[:, :1]) * torch.cos(x[:, 1:])
        p = pc.show(run, net, pc.Sample(x=x, y=y, mask=every), seconds=SHOWN)
        losses.append(nn.functional.mse_loss(p["y_hat"], y).item())  # before learning
        if i == 0 or (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
            recent = losses[-50:]
            mean = sum(recent) / len(recent)
            print(
                f"batch {i + 1:3d}: loss {mean:.4f} (the mean of the last {len(recent)})"
            )
    # The state of a node, by its path: input, layer0, layer1, output.
    lam = run.state_dict()["nodes"]["layer0"]["state"]["lam"]
print(f"the mean |lam| of layer0 (its credit) at the end: {lam.abs().mean():.2e}")

docs.title: ✨ 特徴
docs.text:
• 🔄 推論と学習を同時に: 学習のモードも推論のモードも、エポックも無い
  • 🧩 PyTorch で書くノード: 各ノードは PyTorch で書き実行する
  • ⚡ 非同期のノード: 各ノードは自分の周期で更新し、ほかのノードを待たない
  • ⏱️ 連続時間: 実際に経った時間 dt に比例して更新する
  • 🧠 更新則は自由: ノードの中の BP、ノードをまたぐ PC-ALM、自作の則
  • 💾 状態を保存: ネットワークの状態を取得、後でその状態から再開
  • 🧪 決定的なテスト: 仮想のタイマーと手動の更新でノードをテスト可能
